findings.title: Worker::end runs the teardown sequence twice
findings.expected: A consuming end operation should report the result of its one completed teardown attempt.
findings.observed: end computes the result of finish and then Rust drops the consumed Worker. Drop calls finish again. When the first wait fails, a second grace period can run, and its result is discarded.
findings.impact: The return value can say the child is still alive after the second attempt reaped it. Shutdown can also take an additional grace period. The Linux test permits a 2.5-second window for a one-second refusal.
findings.recommendedFix: Make finalization one-shot. Preserve or explicitly transfer the ability to reap a child that outlives a refused termination.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover one finalization attempt on refusal and a child that exits between the two deadlines. Check the returned status and wait count.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

findings.title: Safe Unix worker bootstrap can close descriptors still owned by application code
findings.expected: A safe entry point must respect live Rust I/O ownership or structurally establish exclusive bootstrap before it touches descriptors.
findings.observed: serve trusts an environment marker to enter worker mode. Unix cleanup closes descriptors above stderr without checking who owns them. A later or repeated call in a host with live File or OwnedFd values can invalidate them. First entry in a fresh, single-threaded worker is the intended case.
findings.impact: Previously opened files or pipes can become unusable. If a descriptor number is reused, a stale owner can act on or close another resource. The current first-call documentation alone cannot express this invariant of a safe function.
findings.recommendedFix: Move cleanup to a controlled pre-application launch phase. Make bootstrap single-use and ensure that only genuinely inherited descriptors are closed. Any externally assumed ownership invariant needs an appropriate API boundary.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise bootstrap with existing application-owned resources using a harmless ownership model. Verify normal fresh startup, refusal of repeat entry, and that the live owner retains its original resource.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

findings.title: The allocation gate ignores failure to block signals
findings.expected: The secretmem gate requires signals to have been blocked before registration and acquisition.
findings.observed: The result of pthread_sigmask is ignored. Under a host policy refusing the operation, the code enters the gate anyway. If the same thread is interrupted by a handler that forks, the fork prepare handler can wait on that very thread.
findings.impact: In this conditional Unix integration the process can hang despite the allocation-side timeout. No disclosure was established.
findings.recommendedFix: Check mask establishment before acquiring the gate and fall back to anonymous pages on refusal. Define how to handle failure to restore the previous mask.
findings.requiredVerification: Test the refused-mask decision with a substitute OS-call result. Confirm the secretmem branch cannot be entered without an established mask.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

findings.title: The terminal worker API claims it disables echo
findings.expected: A caller needs to know who configures and verifies hidden input before requesting a password.
findings.observed: start_on_terminal preserves stderr and the controlling terminal. It contains no password reader or termios change. The public text says that it turns echo off. The implementation can also inherit redirected stderr.
findings.impact: An application using an ordinary terminal read in reliance on this promise may echo a password. The library itself does not read or display one during startup.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe echo setup, verification and restoration as responsibilities of the application reader. Update the wording or introduce an explicit reader with its own guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: Review the public example with a TTY and redirected stderr, using public text. If a hidden reader is later introduced, check the actual terminal state before and after input.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

findings.title: The Linux file-change outcome differs from the documented external-denial case
findings.expected: The documentation and the returned five-state status should agree.
findings.observed: The guide groups NoFileChanges with NoNewSockets and says an external denial without the crate filter yields Unknown. NoFileChanges instead returns Refused whenever the filter is absent and does not probe on that path.
findings.impact: Strict callers reject both, but diagnostics can incorrectly tell users what was established about their environment.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify the intended file-change status separately or implement the documented proof distinction.
findings.requiredVerification: Assert the selected outcome without a local filter and compare the public descriptions with the returned status.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

findings.title: A failed grandchild creation or wait can pass the same-PID regression
findings.expected: When a regression tests a grandchild result, it must establish that the grandchild was created and its status was collected.
findings.observed: Inside the nested-namespace branch the test initializes status to zero and does not check for a failed fork or the return of waitpid before using status. A failure can therefore be reported as a successful child result.
findings.impact: The green top-level check is weaker evidence of the same-PID subcase than its name suggests. This affects the test, not the fork-wiped marker implementation.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a positive child PID and successful waiting for that exact PID before evaluating its termination. Report unavailable prerequisites explicitly.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the successful path and deliberate harness-side launch/wait refusal. An uncollected result must not count as a passed assertion.
findings.reproduction: Static control-flow/contract inspection at the frozen commit. No stand-alone vulnerability reproduction was run.

remediation.title: Linux secret-memory allocation and concurrent fork share an inheritance window
remediation.evidence: The first gate decision is now made with signals masked and only a single thread visible. Late first use selects anonymous pages. The cold-start case ran and the warm secretmem fork loop executed 2,000 iterations. That closes the original ordinary registration race under a successful signal mask. The separate refusal case has a new ID.

remediation.title: Unix worker acknowledges isolation after incomplete descriptor cleanup
remediation.evidence: A clean handshake is required before a request. Linux regression cases cover failed enumeration, detachment and early death. The new finding about late safe-API entry concerns ownership, not an incomplete cleanup being accepted.

remediation.title: Linux tracer evidence for one thread is reported process-wide
remediation.evidence: The implementation reads all visible task statuses. The same-namespace and sibling tracer regressions passed. Namespace visibility is explicitly gated separately.

remediation.title: Windows worker pipe ends are briefly inheritable by unrelated launches
remediation.evidence: Windows still marks the worker pipe ends inheritable across CreateProcessW. The crate lock does not serialize other process launchers in the host. Scope the guarantee or redesign the launch and verify on native Windows. This remains high severity for concurrent inheriting hosts.

remediation.title: macOS accepts local probe denials without a confirmed sandbox profile
remediation.evidence: The macOS profile must have been accepted for default-deny probes to confirm. The new lock serializes initialization. No macOS runtime result.

remediation.title: Signal-domain isolation can satisfy a stricter self-only claim
remediation.evidence: Signal scope and self-only policy are distinct fields. Linux option and inherited-filter tests passed. Provenance across different thread filters remains AUD-003-SEC003.

remediation.title: Unsupported speculation control is accepted as confirmed mitigation
remediation.evidence: The Linux parser distinguishes missing and disabled speculation control. Linux parser/role tests passed. Physical AArch64 hardware was not exercised.

remediation.title: Protected stack properties cannot be required before secret work
remediation.evidence: Required stack properties are checked before pthread_create. Native Linux suite covers the lock-limit and protected-stack callback cases.

remediation.title: Stack wiping assumes every post-pthread byte is an initialized Rust u8
remediation.evidence: Uninitialized bytes are wiped through MaybeUninit, after joining the thread. Targeted Miri passed. The optimized x86-64 Pages::wipe_any code retains byte-zero stores, including the tail.

remediation.title: ClosedSecret forgets the previous access mode after a refused reseal
remediation.evidence: ClosedSecret retains the previous actual access when the OS refuses a transition. The Linux refusal unit case passed. WASM runtime correctly exposes is_closed as false.

remediation.title: Windows dynamic-code status ignores permitted exemptions
remediation.evidence: Windows readback excludes the dynamic-code opt-out and downgrade policy bits. Native execution remains outstanding.

remediation.title: Dropping a worker can wait forever after rejecting a large reply
remediation.evidence: The original large-answer pipe deadlock is covered on Linux. Rejection closes pipes and the 4 MiB regression passed. Teardown status and duplicate finalization are tracked separately.

remediation.title: Fork-based work inside a protected stack may lose its active stack
remediation.evidence: Unix spawns from a helper thread with an ordinary stack. The protected-stack public regression passed on the host. No old-glibc fork fallback was executed.

remediation.title: MemoryLocked loses a successful process lock on re-entry
remediation.evidence: On a host where mlockall succeeds but the fork-wiped status marker cannot be created, a later default call reports NotRequested for the still-effective lock. The initialization caches a failed marker allocation or advice. The current kernel exercises the supported-marker path. Record an indeterminate state or implement a fork-safe readback fallback. This is a false negative and can block strict work. This is possible on Linux 4.4–4.13, or when the marker mapping/advice is refused independently of mlockall.

remediation.title: open_channels can return an apparently complete partial inventory
remediation.evidence: Enumeration returns an error or marks the inventory incomplete on unreadable entries. The normal and incomplete Linux cases passed.

remediation.title: Detailed protection reports describe possible proofs as if observed
remediation.evidence: Proof text derives from the recorded outcome, with Linux serialization and evidence checks passing. Windows-specific runtime proof remains outstanding.

remediation.title: Oversized protected stack requests overflow during rounding
remediation.evidence: Oversized stack requests return an error. The stock Linux unit regression passed.

remediation.title: Hard-coded MCL_ONFAULT is incorrect on some Linux architectures
remediation.evidence: The correct platform libc MCL_ONFAULT constant is used. The configured targets compile. No native execution on a non-host architecture with a different flag value.

remediation.title: Windows work areas skip a potentially available page lock
remediation.evidence: Windows attempts VirtualLock for work areas even if working-set expansion fails. Cross-target Clippy passed. Native execution remains outstanding.

remediation.title: Windows cleanup is attempted on a potentially uninitialized attribute list
remediation.evidence: The Windows attribute-list destructor is reached only after successful initialization. Cross-target Clippy passed. No native failure-path run.

remediation.title: Keystroke serialization leaves wiping to a caller that is promised a wipe
remediation.evidence: KeystrokeBytes owns and wipes the serialized scratch in Drop. Encoding and redacted Debug passed on Linux.

remediation.title: Usage guidance overstates disk guarantees and lists shipped restrictions as planned
remediation.evidence: The initial disk and planned-option descriptions were corrected. The current README documents limits on abrupt exit and global disk guarantees. Current terminal wording has a separate finding.

remediation.title: Worker keeps inherited channels when both descriptor-closing methods fail
remediation.evidence: The Unix cleanup/handshake fix is covered by the Linux regression that refuses admission when the descriptor listing cannot be trusted. Same historical fault as AUD-001-SEC002.

remediation.title: Sequential namespace calls leave IPC shared while network isolation succeeds
remediation.evidence: The combined namespace request remains in place and the stock Linux isolation suite passed. This is the original network/IPC case and is distinct from PID visibility.

remediation.title: Several advertised Windows protections discard their read-back results
remediation.evidence: The Windows job, integrity and policy outcomes now participate in the public report. Native Windows runtime remains outstanding. See AUD-004-SEC001 for the DLL contract.

remediation.title: Dropping a worker after an oversized answer can deadlock both processes
remediation.evidence: Linux regression passed with a rejected oversized reply. Corresponds to AUD-001-FUN001.

remediation.title: Overflowing protected-stack size panics instead of returning an error
remediation.evidence: Oversized protected-stack requests have a passing Linux regression. Corresponds to AUD-001-FUN003.

remediation.title: Technical notes still describe shipped options as future work
remediation.evidence: The technical guide describes the optional restrictions and all three integration executables. The sanitizer and coverage limits are recorded separately.

remediation.title: A selective host policy can satisfy strict socket checks
remediation.evidence: The crate's effective filter or relevant option bit and a denied probe are both required for sockets, program launch, file locks and sendmsg. A foreign denial alone produces Unknown. Native Linux external-policy and unit regressions passed. Android shares the decision logic and was cross-checked only.

remediation.title: A tracer can be invisible to the procfs PID namespace
remediation.evidence: The active PID namespace is checked before confirming absence of a tracer. The Linux profile recorded execution of the nested-namespace comparison to Unknown. Ordinary visible tracer cases also passed. A container using the initial PID namespace is not automatically Unknown merely because it is a container.

remediation.title: Signal-filter ownership is recorded before installation succeeds
remediation.evidence: A refused installation now leaves the signal owner unchanged and the single-threaded failure regression passed. The owner PID is still shared across a process while a successful policy update applies to the calling thread. Sibling threads can retain different inherited rules and read the same affirmative owner. Strict mode can consequently confirm the wrong effective target. Track ownership with the actual per-thread filter and account for descendants.

remediation.title: Worker teardown can wait indefinitely after termination is requested
remediation.evidence: Unix and Windows final waits are bounded. The denied-kill and cooperative large-response cases passed on Linux. Native Windows pending. The new duplicate finalization issue is AUD-006-FUN001 and does not restore the old infinite wait.

remediation.title: A previously refused Landlock layer is not retried on identical entry
remediation.evidence: The missing layer is retried before comparing filter bits. The Linux regression executed the successful retry and the next unchanged entry without stacking additional filters.

remediation.title: The technical notes describe an obsolete seccomp marker
remediation.evidence: The technical notes now give marker base 0xE00 and its option bits. This matches the implementation.

remediation.title: A fatal child sanitizer diagnostic can coexist with a green test run
remediation.evidence: Fresh ASan ran 53 stock checks with four lock-sensitive exclusions. No AddressSanitizer or LeakSanitizer diagnostic appeared. The test executables disable leak detection for the isolated workers. This verifies the specific fatal child diagnostic was eliminated, not leak freedom.

remediation.title: Default DLL search policy is presented as a universal allow-list
remediation.evidence: The rename and explicit-path exception narrow the claim. The public field still promises that every unqualified name uses only two directories. Windows can override default directories with per-call search flags even for a bare name. The technical overview still describes a universal restriction. State the default-search guarantee and avoid treating it as a strict allow-list.

remediation.title: Concurrent macOS isolation calls can erase confirmation of the sandbox
remediation.evidence: Initialization is serialized and success is published monotonically. The Apple targets type-check. Concurrent macOS runtime evidence remains outstanding.

remediation.title: The child-process policy ignores its secure-process exception
remediation.evidence: The child-process readback rejects the secure-process exception bit. Native Windows pending.

remediation.title: ClosedSecret availability of page sealing is overstated
remediation.evidence: The type and documentation describe fallible page sealing and refer to is_closed. Linux refusal regression and a linked WASM runtime case passed.

remediation.title: Existing Windows job need not confirm the documented one-process limit
remediation.evidence: Both the UI restriction set and the active-process limit flag/count are read back for an existing Windows job. Native execution is pending. Job membership and breakaway policy limit the wider claim about children.

independentReviewerItems: Verified for a marked worker on Linux. The startup guard refuses a recursive launch. It does not establish safe descriptor ownership for late or repeated serve.
Allocation while a fork handler waits on the caller
The existing Linux contention regression used the anonymous fallback. LLVM recorded the fallback assertion. The separate signal-mask failure case is AUD-006-FUN002.
Equal numeric PIDs across namespace generations

The implementation replaces numeric PID ownership for the memory lock with a fork-wiped marker. The measured run entered nested namespaces and reached the grandchild creation and collection lines. The unchecked collection prevents a strong per-run verdict for the innermost result. Loss of a marker on some kernels is covered by AUD-001-API001.
Terminal settings on a later-opened device
The guide records the restricted later-opened terminal and the use of an inherited terminal descriptor for a caller-provided reader. The public claim that this API turns off echo is incorrect.
additionalContext: Secret::with_capacity and Secret::zeroed use best-effort page locking when kernel secret memory is unavailable. For a buffer that must remain out of swap, use Secret::locked and check its Result before filling it. Internal worker request and response allocation uses Secret::zeroed. Choosing a strict constructor only for a caller-owned buffer does not enforce a lock for those IPC allocations.

The Windows child-policy exception and both active-process/UI job limits have source changes. A pre-existing job can have breakaway settings. Its one-member limit is a claim about processes associated with the job and does not on its own prove universal child-process prevention.
Snapshot-specific line references can be inspected with git show f3c2401:<path>. The post-build working-tree edits and any later commits need their own verification.
limitations: Native Linux x86-64 on kernel 7.0.0-43-generic and a linked wasm32-unknown-unknown module in Node/V8 were executed. Clippy checked six triples. macOS, iOS, Windows, Android and an old-glibc runtime did not execute. A Linux build of Windows source cannot verify AppContainer, job or inheritance behavior.

The measured LLVM percentage excludes non-Linux code and worker-side paths that cannot emit profiles after the deliberate environment reset. Four lock-dependent cases were excluded under ASan. Leak checking is disabled in the test binaries. Coverage is evidence of execution, not a security guarantee.

The 31 mutation reversions and the reported seven historical disclosures in 400 trials were not independently replayed. The repository was frozen and the audit did not modify any production code. No secret data was used.

Boundary cases in findings are reported from source, contract checks and public documented OS semantics. No end-to-end secret disclosure, pentest, leak-freedom proof or native foreign security certification is claimed.
Current advisory results are bound to the local database. No new dependency internals, consumer GUI, package deployment, hibernation, VM snapshots, or privileged operating-system access were audited.
